title: Microsegment Fade Strategy Composer and Contextual Undo Flow
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design a surface in Redwood Console to create and visualize 'microsegment fade' strategies for staged rollouts and to provide a contextual 'Undo' (contextual rollback) experience. The goal is to let engineers compose phased traffic fades across tiny audience cohorts, preview downstream effects (latency/cost/quality), and have an explainable, reversible undo action with rationale capture for audit and incident postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: Composer UI allows selection of multiple microsegments (by attribute filters) and chaining fade steps with duration and concurrency knobs.
Preview pane simulates traffic redistribution over time and surface key metrics (p95 latency delta, tokens/sec cost delta, error rate) for each step.

Contextual Undo flow anchors to a rollout step and presents: reason capture, suggested rollback target (partial or full), estimated impact, and one-click rollback action with confirm and audit log entry.
Design aligns with accessibility standards (keyboard flows + screen reader labels) and fits within existing console visual language.
Prototype includes microinteraction for 'fade vs cut' toggles and a timeline scrubber for manual replay.
Edge case flows documented: concurrent rollouts, overlapping segments, and autoscale-triggered fallback.
Handoff artifacts (Figma frames + annotated spec) reviewed and approved by PM and Eng leads.
decisions: Use attribute-filter based microsegments (user_id cohort, region, device, custom tags) instead of free 'percentage-of-traffic' only to support precise audience targeting.
Expose both 'fade' (gradual percentage ramp) and 'cut' (immediate switch) controls; default to fade with conservative ramp presets.
Contextual Undo will create a rollback action tied to the current variant version and snapshot runtime metrics at time of decision for auditability.
Preview simulations will use last 24h traffic distribution and conservatively estimate cost/latency changes using heuristics from Optimize service.
Timeline scrubber is the canonical place to review event-by-event state when composing or debugging a rollout.
tradeoffs: Simulation accuracy vs speed: we use heuristics for fast previews; deep-sim (hour-long replays) is out of scope for v1.
Composer complexity vs discoverability: exposing many knobs increases power for advanced users but risks overwhelming new users. We'll hide advanced controls behind an 'advanced' toggle.
Storing rationale for every undo could increase audit log volume; we'll compress long-form text and index only metadata for search.
